messages.text: Can the Magic M. 40T be run even lower than the Eco mode? Also, why is the price on the 40T the same as the Harlo B30. For the same money what does your team recommend between the two, beyond the Hash rate?
Read the magic miner 40t page
Read the bsb b30 page
Use the catalog search.
Searched the catalog · Magic M. 40T Harlo B30

Quick correction first: the 40T is $799 and the B30 is $899 on the live listing, so the 40T is actually $100 cheaper.

On going below Eco: Eco is the lowest preset in the 40T's stock firmware, about 30 TH/s at roughly 450 W. I can't confirm anything lower than that. I can ask our hardware lead if you'd like.

Since you're reading the heat-your-home piece, here's the honest split. The 40T is the better value at about $19 per TH, and it has Ethernet plus dual-band Wi-Fi. Its floor is about 450 W, though, and it runs around 50 dB in Eco.

The B30 can go much lower: 18 TH/s at 230 W in ECO, at about 50 dB. In that mode it's also the more efficient of the two, at 12.8 J/TH. Its Wi-Fi is 2.4 GHz only, with Ethernet as well.

Our pick: if you want the most hashrate and heat for the money, get the 40T. If it's going in a smaller room where you want a gentler, lower-draw heater, get the B30. Which sounds more like your space?
Yes, please ask your hardware lead. I don't want it for a heater. I live in Arizona
Handed to the team · Neither spec is in the product facts. Team is closed, so the answer goes to the

I've sent your question to our hardware lead. I also asked for the highest room temperature each unit is rated to run in, since neither spec is on the listings. The team is offline right now. They'll pick it up today at 10am ET and send the answer to (email hidden)

In Arizona, every watt the miner draws ends up as heat in the room, and your AC has to remove it. That favours the B30. It can run at 230 W in ECO, while the 40T's lowest preset is about 450 W. The 40T still gets you more hashrate per dollar. Where would it sit: inside the house or in a garage?
thank you
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: since it isn't for heating, what matters most to you in a miner?

Sound lever first, power efficiency second, as I plan to run this off surplus solar, but I only have so much surplus solar and why I would like to run it below the eco modes, especially in the summer when I have less solar and struggle to keep my house cool.

That points to the B30. Its ECO mode draws 230 W at the wall for 18 TH/s, which is 12.8 J/TH, the most efficient mode we list on either unit. The 40T can't drop below about 450 W, and that much power also means more heat in your house in summer.

On sound, both are listed at around 50 dB. That's the B30's single listed figure and the 40T's Eco number.

How much surplus solar do you usually have on a summer afternoon?
I like the 40T because I get more hash rate at a $100 savings

You're right that the 40T gives you more hashrate for less money. That's why it's the best value we sell.

The catch for your setup is the power floor. The 40T needs about 450 W even in Eco, which works out to about 15 J/TH. On days your surplus solar drops below 450 W, it would be pulling from the grid. The B30 can drop to 230 W at 12.8 J/TH.

If our hardware lead confirms the 40T can run below Eco, it's the clear pick for you. I'd wait for that answer, which goes to your email, before ordering.
I will be anxiously awaiting to hear from the hardware lead. Would love to run it at higher rates during the winter, and lower than Eco in the summer

That makes sense. For the winter half, the 40T already handles it. Turbo runs about 42 TH/s at roughly 690 W, and that's normal use. Going above 42 TH/s is overclocking, which is at your own risk and may affect warranty coverage if it causes damage. The B30 tops out at 30 TH/s at 485 W.

So the open question is just the summer floor. Our hardware lead picks it up today from 10am ET, and the answer will come to (email hidden) Thanks for laying out your setup so clearly.
I know electronics, and I would never overclock. I want longevity over max Th/s

Understood, and that's a sensible way to run any miner.

Here's a detail you'll appreciate. The 40T has 30 BM1370 chips, and each chip runs comfortably at 1.2 to 1.5 TH/s. Eco works out to about 1.0 TH/s per chip, Standard 1.2 and Turbo 1.4. So even Turbo stays inside that comfortable range, and Eco sits below it.

I've already asked our hardware lead about running below Eco, and the answer will come to your email.
That is amazing. I am all done. Thank you for your proficiency tonight. Bye
Thanks, it was a pleasure. You'll get the hardware lead's answer about running below Eco at (email hidden) Enjoy the rest of your night, and good luck with the solar setup.
